graphEvents.label: why hand-written table rows stay pending
consumed rows are produced only by the save writer
writer reuses ids only through appendix items

label: Pending is defined as the session queue minus consumed.jsonl keys and nothing else, so any answer without a consumed row is pending by construction.

The only non-test producer of a consumed row is writePlannedOperatorDecisions, which hands result.ids from writeDecisionRecord to recordConsumedKeys; it never reads a decision record to discover that an answer is already recorded there.

A hand-written table row contributes no entry to the save, therefore no id, therefore no consumed row: the gap opens before matching, because the save is never handed an entry for a decision recorded elsewhere.

The writer has exactly two id-reuse paths, a source comment under an appendix heading and an unkeyed appendix item matched on normalized question plus answer; a table row is neither, and no code reads a table row's text.
The writer's own decisions table has five columns and no answer column, so answer-text matching is structurally impossible against any table the writer produces.
Live state for session fe0c9990-06d3-454e-a8e7-7c7bc649bc49: 35 queue records, 2 consumed keys, 33 pending, nudge cursor 29, and exactly one session queue file on disk.

The packet decision record carries four source-keyed appendix items (Q001-Q004) while consumed.jsonl holds two keys: the two chat-keyed items reached the record without the writer, so their keys were never consumed and the sweep still prints them as chat candidates. Cause inferred; artifact state confirmed.

Queue files are session-scoped and nothing in the hook directory enumerates the queue directory, so a session whose answers were never consumed leaves an orphan queue file that no later session's sweep can read.

The Stop-hook message names only /speckit:save --full-auto, while planOperatorDecisions returns null with no log at zero entries; the sweep that produces entries is documented only in save.md, so the instruction can be followed to completion with every record still pending.

Contradiction with 002's framing: takeNudge reports once per pending-count increase and lowers the cursor silently, so the recurring real-use surface is the sweep's pending list at each save, not a repeating Stop nudge. 002's fix is unaffected; the acceptance wording should change.

The Claude adapter falls back to process.cwd() when neither CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR nor payload.cwd is set, contradicting the core's stated invariant that no path resolves from the process working directory.

Appendix parsing accepts one style only: FIELD_LABEL_RE anchors Question:/Options:/Answer: at column 0 with no bold or indent, so a hand-written appendix using a different label style is invisible to the unkeyed matching path; the text comparison normalizes case and internal whitespace only.

A re-save can leave a table row and its appendix disagreeing: insertDecisionRow replaces a known id's row while insertAppendixItem returns lines unchanged once the heading exists, and the new key is then marked consumed.

Consumed rows record only key, packet, id and timestamp with no answer text and no release path, so a wrong mapping is undetectable from the log and cannot be undone without hand-editing gitignored state.

Capture is silent by design when it drops a decision: an unrecognized answers shape yields zero records, a product question whose header matches the process patterns is discarded with no trace, and multi-select answers are joined with a comma that no later reader can distinguish from a single option.

The writer's suite covers keyed reuse and unkeyed appendix reuse plus a negative question-only case, but nothing covers a hand-written table row because that capability does not exist; 002 adds a capability and a test surface, not a regression fix.

002's read-only side matcher plus CLI appending consumed rows through recordConsumedKeys, guarded by a sha256 check and an answer gate, targets the traced cause without writing into another repository, and correctly rejects routing a save at the foreign packet.

Four gaps 002 leaves open: the consumed mapping is per-machine because it lives in gitignored state, nothing invokes the matcher from the documented save path, refusals must be counted rather than aiming at pending zero, and findings 7, 8, 13 and 14 are owned by no child.

A captured answer only stops counting as pending when its source key enters consumed.jsonl, and only two code paths can put it there: a save that was handed the entry, and a matcher that appends a matched row.
Id reuse inside a decision record requires an appendix item, either with a source comment or with matchable question and answer text; no table row can bind a key.
Pending is session-scoped while consumed is project-scoped, so an unconsumed answer is only ever offered again through a sweep pointed at its own session transcript.
Every capture path resolves under the caller's project directory and never from the process working directory.
